videos.title: 21.10.26 - Ep.26 - The Architecture of Market Liquidity
videos.summary_source_text:
21.10.26 - Ep.26 - The Architecture of Market Liquidity What happens when you press Buy or Sell? Episode 26 explores order books, bid-ask spreads, market depth, execution and why the price on your screen may not be the price you receive.

PRICE IS NOT LIQUIDITY

A displayed price tells you where an asset is trading, but not how much you can trade at that level, how quickly your order will fill, or how much it might move the market. Every order interacts with available liquidity on the opposite side. If there is insufficient size at the best price, it may execute across several levels.

THE FOUR DIMENSIONS OF LIQUIDITY

Liquidity is more than trading volume. We explore four important dimensions:

• Tightness — the cost of crossing between buyers and sellers, most visibly represented by the bid-ask spread.
• Depth — how much buying and selling interest is available around the current price.
• Immediacy — how quickly an order can be executed.
• Resiliency — how quickly the market recovers after liquidity is consumed and prices are pushed away from their previous levels.

A market can have a narrow spread but little depth. High turnover does not mean unlimited liquidity at every price.

UNDERSTANDING THE ORDER BOOK

An order book displays buying interest (bids) and selling interest (asks) at different prices. The best bid is the highest available buying price; the best ask is the lowest available selling price. The difference is the spread.

The mid-price — halfway between the best bid and ask — is a useful reference, but not necessarily an immediately executable price.

DEPTH, ORDER SIZE & MARKET IMPACT

The order book forms a staircase of available liquidity. A small order may be filled entirely at the best available price. A larger market order can consume that liquidity and continue into higher ask prices when buying, or lower bid prices when selling.

This is how the average execution price can differ from the price initially displayed. The larger your order relative to available depth, the greater the potential market impact. Liquidity is relative to trade size: a market that feels liquid to a retail trader may be difficult for an institution placing a large order.

WHY EXECUTION MATTERS

Two traders can buy the same asset at the same moment but receive different average prices if their order sizes differ. Large investors must consider how orders consume liquidity and may reveal demand.

We also look at ticks — the minimum price increments in a market — and why understanding tick value matters, particularly when trading leveraged contracts. A small price movement can mean a significant gain or loss depending on contract size and quantity. Fees, spreads and slippage also affect the result.

MARKET ORDERS VS. LIMIT ORDERS

A market order prioritises execution against available liquidity, but the final price is not guaranteed to match the last price shown on the chart. A large order may fill in parts at different prices.

A limit order gives you more control over the price: a buy limit sets the maximum price you are willing to pay, while a sell limit sets the minimum price you are willing to accept. However, the order may not fill if the market does not reach your price or available orders do not match.

Market orders generally offer greater execution certainty but less price certainty. Limit orders offer greater price control but less certainty of execution. Neither is automatically better; the right choice depends on urgency, volatility, liquidity, trade size and strategy.

THE LAST PRICE IS NOT YOUR PRICE

Charts commonly display trades that have already happened. When you submit an order, you interact with the market as it exists at that moment — including the current bid and ask, available depth, competing orders, volatility, order size and execution speed.

The gap between expected and actual execution matters especially for large trades and transfers between platforms or networks.

THE KEY TAKEAWAY

Trading is not only about predicting direction. It is also about how efficiently you can enter and exit. Understanding the order book, spread, depth, order types and market impact helps explain why the displayed price and your actual execution may differ.

Before pressing Buy or Sell, ask not only “What is the price?” but also “How much liquidity is available, what will my order cost, and how might it be filled?”

Next, we continue with the relationship between analysis and execution, and explore more of the mechanics that shape the trades we actually receive.

videos.title: Hindi - 21.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 21.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

There's No Need To Panic | Grades For the First 10 Games Colorado Avalanche fans hit panic mode after back-to-back losses, but is concern justified just ten games into the NHL season? Brady Tkachuk: Scores Goal, But Florida Panthers Lose to Senators in Return to Ottawa Florida Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk speaks to the media in Ottawa after his team lost 5-1 to the Senators on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. 

Tkachuk spent eight seasons with the Senators — the last five as captain — before asking for a trade and working his way to the Panthers. 

He scored the first goal in the game only to see Ottawa score the next five. 

The Panthers (5-3-2) had won three straight; they visit Pittsburgh on Thursday.

videos.summary_source_text:
The #1 Vitamin for Swollen Legs and Ankles (It's Not Vitamin D or Vitamin E) Vitamin B1 plays an important role in the nervous system and the vascular system, including the muscle control involved in normal circulation and fluid balance. When B1 is low, that loss of control can contribute to swelling and edema in the legs and ankles.

If you want more help with this topic, watch this video here: ▶️ https://youtu.be/TBSGhpG8yfE

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4zIJrNm

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.   

One of the biggest reasons for low vitamin B1 is a diet high in refined carbohydrates. Sugar and starch increase the body’s demand for B1 because this vitamin is required for carbohydrate metabolism.

If you’re dealing with swollen legs or ankles, consider both:

• Increasing vitamin B1
• Reducing refined sugars and starches

videos.summary_source_text:
Do This Before Bed to Calm Your Nerves, Relax Your Body & Sleep Better!  Dr. Mandell Are you going to bed exhausted, yet your body still feels tense, restless, and unable to relax? What if one simple nighttime ritual could help calm your nervous system, ease muscle tension, improve circulation in your feet, and prepare your body for deeper, more restful sleep? In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell reveals a soothing bedtime routine using warm water and Epsom salt (magnesium sulfate) that may help your body unwind naturally. Discover how warmth can encourage blood flow, relax tired feet and legs, ease everyday stress, and support the body's natural transition into rest and relaxation. When your mind is racing, your muscles feel tight, or your body simply won't settle down, this easy nighttime practice may help you feel calmer and more comfortable before sleep. Learn why relaxation before bedtime is so important for your nervous system, sleep quality, and overall well-being. Sometimes the simplest changes to your evening routine can make a meaningful difference in how you feel. Give your body the opportunity to slow down, release tension, and prepare for a peaceful night's rest. Please share this video with your friends and loved ones, and remember to make it a great day! videos.title: Paul Maurice, Panthers Pregame: Brady Tkachuk Returns to Face Ottawa Senators
videos.summary_source_text:
Paul Maurice, Panthers Pregame: Brady Tkachuk Returns to Face Ottawa Senators Florida Panthers coach Paul Maurice speaks to the media in Ottawa before his team faces the Senators on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. 

Brady Tkachuk spent eight seasons with the Senators — the last five as captain — before asking for a trade and working his way to the Panthers. 

Florida will be without goalie Jacob Markstrom for 10-14 days after he left practice early Monday. 

The Panthers (5-2-2) have won three straight after beating Seattle 8-3 on Saturday. Carter Verhaeghe got  a natural hat trick; that was Florida’s third such feat in the past three games which no NHL team had ever done. 

Sam Bennett also had a hat trick — the first time Florida had two such games in the same contest. 

The Panthers hit the road this coming week visiting the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday in Brady Tkachuk’s return to the Canadian Capital. 

Tkachuk was named the NHL’s First Star of the Week after having the first two natural hat tricks last week.

Video Courtesy Florida Panthers / @FlaPanthers / Panthers Vision

videos.title: Brady Tkachuk Meets Media in Return to Ottawa with the Florida Panthers
videos.summary_source_text:
Brady Tkachuk Meets Media in Return to Ottawa with the Florida Panthers Florida Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk speaks to the media in Ottawa upon his return to face the Senators on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. 

Tkachuk spent eight seasons with the Senators — the last five as captain — before asking for a trade and working his way to the Panthers. 

Florida will be without goalie Jacob Markstrom for 10-14 days after he left practice early Monday. 

The Panthers (5-2-2) have won three straight after beating Seattle 8-3 on Saturday. Carter Verhaeghe got  a natural hat trick; that was Florida’s third such feat in the past three games which no NHL team had ever done. 

Sam Bennett also had a hat trick — the first time Florida had two such games in the same contest. 

The Panthers hit the road this coming week visiting the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday in Brady Tkachuk’s return to the Canadian Capital. 

Tkachuk was named the NHL’s First Star of the Week after having the first two natural hat tricks last week.

Video Courtesy Florida Panthers / @FlaPanthers / Panthers Vision

videos.title: Google’s Gemini 5: A 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade!
videos.summary_source_text:
Google’s Gemini 5: A 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade! Gemini 5 rumors are exploding, but is Google actually preparing its next-generation AI model? A reported internal model called Carbon is fueling speculation, with one Google employee comparing its coding abilities to Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5. Meanwhile, Gemini 4 Argon is already delivering impressive benchmark results, a massive one-million-token context window, and powerful AI agent capabilities.

But there's a problem: Google hasn't announced Gemini 5, and the available evidence tells a much more complicated story.

Google's recent release pace has been remarkable. Gemini 3.6 Flash scored 49% on DeepSWE, followed by Gemini 3.7 Flash at 65.3%, Gemini 3.8 Flash at 74%, and Gemini 4 Argon at 77.9%. That's rapid progress, but the improvements are getting smaller. Is Google approaching diminishing returns, or preparing something fundamentally different?

Gemini 4 Argon provides some important clues.

Google's published benchmarks show Argon winning 13 out of 19 comparisons against models including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5. It scores 51.3% on AutomationBench, 65.4% on Vals Finance Agent, and 91.7% on LVBench.

However, independent testing paints a more balanced picture. Artificial Analysis gives Argon an Intelligence Index score of 53, tying GPT-6 Astra. And on Terminal-Bench 4.0, Argon scores just 57.4% compared with Claude Opus 5.5's 66.4%.

That difference matters because real-world AI agents need more than strong reasoning benchmarks. They need to navigate complex environments, execute tools, debug software, and recover when things go wrong.

Then there's the Carbon leak.

According to Business Insider's reporting, Google employees have been testing internal checkpoints named Argon, Barium, and Carbon. One employee reportedly compared Carbon's coding performance to Claude Opus 5.5. But the report describes these as checkpoints within the Gemini 4 family, not confirmation of Gemini 5.

So is Carbon an early Gemini 5 candidate, an improved Gemini 4 model, or something else entirely?

Pricing adds another twist.

Gemini 4 Argon's introductory API pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Starting December 1, those listed prices double to $4 and $20, matching Claude Opus 5.5's pricing while GPT-6.1 Sol remains at $2 and $10.

Meanwhile, Gemini 3.8 Flash may represent Google's more interesting achievement. On the independent DeepSWE leaderboard, it reportedly matches GPT-6 Astra's 74% score at roughly half the cost per problem.

We also examine Google's demonstrations of Argon debugging Android applications, working overnight on Chromium, building 3D environments, generating playable games from video, and creating GPU-powered interfaces.

These demonstrations are impressive, but they depend heavily on specialized agent frameworks like Google's Antigravity. A powerful model isn't automatically an autonomous software engineer.

And even a future Gemini 5 would still need to confront hallucinations, prompt injection, reasoning failures, limited long-term memory, and the difficulties of reliable multi-step autonomy.

What would actually justify calling a model Gemini 5?

A major improvement in terminal-based coding, genuine end-to-end agent autonomy, persistent memory, more unified multimodal intelligence, or a breakthrough in efficiency could matter far more than another benchmark increase.

Google also has an advantage that extends beyond model performance: Android, Search, Chrome, YouTube, Workspace, and its custom AI infrastructure.

The bigger question isn't simply when Gemini 5 will release. It's whether Google can turn its research and ecosystem into AI capabilities that OpenAI and Anthropic cannot easily replicate.

We separate confirmed announcements from reported leaks, compare Gemini 4 Argon with its competitors, examine the December pricing change, and explain what a genuine next-generation Gemini model would have to prove.

CHAPTERS

00:00 Gemini 5 Rumors, Carbon Leaks, and the Release Date Mystery
00:49 Why The Gemini 5 Rumors Feel Believable
02:10 Argon's Lead Is Real, But It's Mostly Google Grading Google
04:52 What The Carbon Leak Actually Shows
06:21 The Price Doubles On December 1
08:13 What Argon Can Do Once Someone Builds The Harness
10:09 The Problems A Bigger Model Won't Fix By Itself
11:15 What A Real Gemini 5 Would Have To Prove

videos.title: Hur leder du medarbetare som utvecklas i olika takt?
videos.summary_source_text:
Hur leder du medarbetare som utvecklas i olika takt? PwC släppte nyligen sin årliga rapport ”Global Workforce Hopes and Fears”, där nästan 50 000 medarbetare i 48 länder har deltagit (varav 1 000 i Sverige). Respondenterna har bland annat svarat på frågor om AI-användande, motivation och sitt förtroende för arbetsgivaren.

Rapporten visar bland annat att trots att svenska företag ligger långt framme när det gäller AI-investeringar, använder svenska medarbetare AI i lägre utsträckning än det globala genomsnittet. Studien visar också att grupper med hög AI-användning upplever större trygghet, högre motivation och bättre utvecklingsmöjligheter än grupper med lägre användning.

Denna tudelning skapar ett nytt och komplext dilemma för chefer och ledare, särskilt för företag och organisationer som behöver engagera hela personalstyrkan i sitt förändringsarbete. Om detta samtalar PwC:s Bonnie Nord och Lisa Haglund med Karin Zingmark i vår sändning. Karin Zingmark är författare och föreläsare inom digital kommunikation, ledarskap och varumärkesbyggande. Hon har också tidigare varit marknadschef på Microsoft i Sverige.

videos.title: 20.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
20.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

videos.summary_source_text:
A Back to Back of Bad Play From the Colorado Avalanche Raises Some Concern Colorado Avalanche stumble with back-to-back losses, raising concerns as scoring woes continue and star forward Nathan MacKinnon battles through an uncharacteristic slump. Are these early struggles a sign of deeper issues, or just a brief October hiccup for a roster packed with talent?

Hosts Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the Avalanche’s disappointing 4-3 defeat to the New Jersey Devils, questioning the team’s lackluster offense, shot generation, and reliance on late goals from Artturi Lehkonen. The discussion spotlights Scott Wedgewood’s stellar goaltending, the impact of missing depth like Logan O’Connor, and how tweaks to the lineup (including the much-maligned 11-and-7 format) have disrupted Colorado's flow. With fans voicing frustration and soundcheck selections capturing the team's mood, the episode explores whether adversity now could build resilience for another Stanley Cup run—or expose cracks the Avs need to fix fast.

Florida will be without goalie Jacob Markstrom for 10-14 days after he left practice early Monday. 

The Panthers (5-2-2) have won three straight after beating Seattle 8-3 on Saturday. Carter Verhaeghe got  a natural hat trick; that was Florida’s third such feat in the past three games which no NHL team had ever done.

BMW’s NEW 7 Series just DESTROYED the Mercedes S-Class… Is the new 7 Series the ultimate luxurious limo?!

The BMW 7 Series has been updated! 

But this is no ordinary facelift. BMW claims it is the biggest facelift it has ever undertaken on any car EVER! In fact, the changes are so extensive, it’s effectively a totally new generation rather than a facelift. 

So does the new 7 Series have what it takes to stand out against its key competitors - the Audi A8 and Mercedes S-Class? Let’s take a look…

In terms of the exterior design, it’s still clearly a 7 Series, but with several differences from the previous iteration. Up top, there’s a completely new front end, with a bigger and more in-your-face grille, along with bigger air intakes. This car has the optional DRLs with 12 crystals included in them, and the grooves in the bonnet are the same as those first introduced in the recent M3. The side view is pretty similar to the past edition, while around the back a lot has changed, with tail lights now just short of running full length, and there’s even a boot lip spoiler - not that it’ll do much, though! 

As for the inside, the changes are once again extensive. There’s a new dash, new screens, new fabrics, a new steering wheel, a new centre console, and the inclusion of the Panoramic Display - it’s basically a whole new interior!  There’s now a passenger screen, an all-new infotainment screen (with all-new software), and pretty much every element you touch is high quality. 

The back seats are also just as premium as they were before. There’s a whole load of customisation in the seats, including a ‘Relaxation Mode’ which reclines the seat and moves the front seats away to offer as much legroom as possible. The Theatre Mode screen has been retained, and it now comes with an 8K display, Dolby Atmos, and it’s now a touchscreen! 

Under the bonnet, you can choose from 3-litre straight-six diesel or petrol engines. The car we have here is the 740, which means it’s a 3-litre straight-six producing 400hp, with that power sent only to the rear wheels. In the future, there’ll also be a 3-litre PHEV with over 600hp, and an all-electric i7 is also due with 680hp. What’s more, there are even rumours of a V8 edition on the horizon!

So is the 7 Series, the ultimate luxury limo? Or would you choose the S-Class instead? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: Google's AI Notebook Is Getting Seriously Powerful — Here's What It Can Do
videos.summary_source_text:
Google's AI Notebook Is Getting Seriously Powerful — Here's What It Can Do Google says its upgraded Gemini Notebook, formerly NotebookLM, beats the previous version in more than 65% of side-by-side comparisons. For web research, that figure jumps to 78.2%. But here's the catch: Google tested its own AI against its own older system. Does that make Gemini Notebook a serious research tool, or just another impressive AI demo?

With more than 30 million users and over 600,000 organizations reportedly using the platform, the stakes are getting higher. Students, researchers, analysts, and businesses are trusting Google's AI to understand documents, analyze data, generate reports, and explain complex information. But how reliable are those answers?

Originally introduced as Project Tailwind at Google I/O 2023, NotebookLM started as an experimental AI notebook that answered questions using your uploaded sources. Now renamed Gemini Notebook, it's evolving into something much more powerful.

The biggest change arrived with Google's June 2026 Gemini 3.5 upgrade. Gemini Notebook can now use a secure cloud computer, write and execute code, analyze spreadsheets, create charts, and generate downloadable files, including Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations, PDFs, CSV, and JSON.

Powered by Google's Antigravity coding technology and more than 100 curated software skills, the platform is moving beyond document summarization toward an AI-powered research and productivity workspace.

And that's not the only transformation.

Gemini Notebook can turn uploaded documents into podcast-style Audio Overviews, narrated Video Overviews, and even Cinematic Video Overviews. The cinematic feature combines Gemini, Nano Banana, and Veo to create animated explanations from your research materials.

It can also work with PDFs, Google Docs, Google Slides, spreadsheets, research papers, websites, and YouTube transcripts. With Google Search integration, users can discover new sources and add them directly to their notebooks.

But there's an important difference between Gemini Notebook and traditional AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity.

Gemini Notebook uses source-grounded answers and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to connect responses to your documents. Its inline citations let you trace claims back to the original material.

That sounds like a solution to AI hallucinations. Unfortunately, it's not that simple.

A citation can point to the wrong passage. The AI can misinterpret numbers, overlook conflicting information, or produce a convincing explanation from incomplete evidence. Even source-grounded AI can make mistakes.

We also examine Google's reported benchmark improvements, including its 69.9% win rate for large-document analysis and 78.2% for web research. These numbers suggest progress, but they are not independent accuracy measurements or proof that Gemini Notebook outperforms competing AI tools.

Then there's pricing and availability.

Google initially limited the Gemini 3.5 cloud computer upgrade to eligible AI Ultra and Workspace customers, with an AI Pro rollout announced later. Free users still face uncertainty around access to the most advanced capabilities. Cinematic Video Overviews also launched with restricted availability.

So who should actually use Gemini Notebook?

We break down practical applications for students studying lecture notes, researchers comparing scientific papers, analysts reviewing business reports, and professionals searching through large document collections. We also explain when traditional research methods, expert judgment, or another AI tool might be the better choice.

The real question isn't whether Gemini Notebook can produce an impressive podcast, animated video, or presentation. It's whether its answers are trustworthy enough to support serious work.

And with Google bringing notebooks into the broader Gemini ecosystem and planning integration with AI Mode in Search, that question is becoming increasingly important.

Watch until the end for a simple test you can run yourself to find out how reliably Gemini Notebook handles conflicting sources.

Have you tried Gemini Notebook or NotebookLM? Does it actually improve your research workflow, or have you caught it making mistakes? Share your experience in the comments.

videos.summary_source_text:
The ONLY 2 Dumbbell Triceps Exercises You Need (NO, SERIOUSLY!) Get big triceps here - https://athleanx.com
Subscribe to the channel here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

What if I told you that here were only 2 dumbbell triceps exercises you need to grow bigger triceps, would you believe me? In this video, I am going to show you how only two dumbbell triceps exercises are all that is required to build big triceps. Remember, it comes down to not only the choice of the exercise you make, but how do them that makes all the difference.

The first exercise out of the only 2 dumbbell triceps exercises you need to build bigger triceps is a variation of an already popular triceps exercise. You might recognize this exercise as the dumbbell overhead triceps extension where you stand in space and hold a single dumbbell behind your head with both hands. This is a great exercise for targeting the long head of the triceps - the head of the muscle that makes up the most size of the triceps.

However, for many with limited shoulder mobility, it causes shoulder discomfort with the arms up overhead and with hands back behind the head. This can be fixed by making one big alteration to the exercise; using an incline bench.

By leaning back against an incline bench, you provide your shoulders with a much more comfortable position where your arms are not directly overhead, but rather slightly in front of you. This eliminates the shoulder discomfort but allows for enough stretch on the long head of the triceps that you will still see the benefits of the exercise. This more natural, comfortable position will also allow you to keep your elbows pointing straight forward instead of flaring them. This means that you are remaining in the scapular plane and are preventing internal rotation of the shoulder joint with elevation.

There is also an added safety factor to this version of the exercise outside of the shoulder positioning that will allow you to keep building big triceps as time goes on. The incline version of this exercise allows for enough clearance so that you don't ever hit your head with the dumbbell at any point in the range of motion. Add in that once you reach failure, you don't have to worry about dropping the dumbbell. Instead, simply slide down the bench and allow the dumbbell to catch itself on the top of the bench where you will easily be able to manipulate the dumbbell in space, safely.

The second exercise of the only 2 dumbbell tricep exercises you need is one you might have stopped doing a long time ago: the tricep kickback. The kickback gets a bad rap from many online influencers and keyboard scientists arguing that active insufficiency makes the exercise worthless. Basically, they are saying that you are actively minimizing the amount of force the triceps can produce and thus you must subjugate yourself to light weights that won't build muscle.

If active insufficiency was a real problem, then we should be avoiding exercises like leg extensions and preacher curls because they don't allow you to lift as much weight as a barbell squat or curl. The argument against the kickback is flawed because muscles don't know what weight is measured on the side of the dumbbell, but instead respond to overall tension. If the triceps are subjected to high tension due to muscle length shortening plus the weight of the dumbbell, we still have an opportunity to build muscle.

The kickback works as perfect compliment to the incline powerbomb because while we have trained the triceps with the long head on stretch, we need an exercise that trains the triceps with the long head in it's most shortened / contracted position. This requires getting the elbow and shoulder into extension (meaning your arm goes back behind your body).

We are going to utilize the incline bench once again, but this time, we are going to lower the incline to about 30 degrees. This is the perfect position to assume the proper posture and arm position required to make the kickback as effective as possible. This incline will allow for your triceps to be perfectly parallel with the floor when you reach the top end of the range of motion.

Hold the rep at the top for a second or two and realize exactly what you've been missing by skipping this incredible triceps exercise.

With those two exercise, you are training the long head of the triceps on stretch and in peak contraction - covering the whole range of motion of the triceps in order to build bigger triceps.

videos.summary_source_text:
19.10.26 - Ep.25 (Part 6) - Capital Behaviour as an Intelligence Layer How does capital move, and why must flow analysis be combined with risk management? We connect capital-flow analysis to RIFT’s Smart Money feature.

SMART MONEY: OBSERVE, DON'T BLINDLY COPY

Smart Money is an intelligence layer for observing capital behaviour, not a promise of profits or an instruction to copy another trader. Study the assets experienced participants trade, their direction, position size, concentration, holding period and leverage. The goal is to evaluate, not blindly follow someone who appears successful.

CAPITAL FLOW + RISK

Episode 24 explored how capital must survive; Episode 25 has followed where capital moves. Flow analysis without risk assessment can encourage reckless chasing, while risk analysis without flow awareness can miss market transitions.

Ask: Is money moving towards an opportunity or away from it? How vulnerable is the exposure if conditions reverse?

Strong inflows are not automatically safe. Leverage, crowded positions, extreme valuations and thin liquidity can make a popular trade fragile. Outflows can sometimes create opportunities, but distinguish temporary liquidity pressure from genuine deterioration in fundamentals.

NOT ALL CAPITAL IS EQUAL

Two rallies can look alike on a chart but have different foundations. One may reflect long-term allocation, spot buying and broad participation; another may depend on leverage, speculation and momentum chasing. The quality and purpose of the flow matter.

Capital operates on different time horizons, from milliseconds for high-frequency strategies to years or decades for pension and sovereign wealth funds. Short-term selling can occur within a long-term uptrend. Always ask whose capital you are observing — retail, institutions, passive funds, hedge funds, market makers or long-term allocators — and what objectives might explain their behaviour.

A CAPITAL-FLOW CHECKLIST

When examining a market, ask:
• Are liquidity and credit conditions expanding or tightening?
• Which currencies, asset classes or sectors are gaining preference?
• Where is positioning concentrated, and how much leverage supports the move?
• Where is money entering or leaving, and how broad is participation?
• What could happen if the flow reverses?

These questions offer a fuller picture than simply asking whether a chart is rising. AI can help organise research, but judgement and evidence still matter.

FOUR TYPES OF CAPITAL FLOW

Market movements can involve several types at once:

Fundamental flow — expectations change because of economic data, policy or rates.

Liquidity flow — financial conditions change the availability or cost of capital.

Positioning flow — traders enter, exit, hedge or rebalance.

Forced flow — liquidations, margin calls, redemptions or risk limits leave participants little choice.

Forced selling can be powerful because survival becomes more important than the original thesis. Persistent structural allocation, driven by technology, demographics, regulation or wider market access, can reshape markets.

PRICE IS ONLY THE STARTING POINT

Price shows the outcome, not the full story. A chart alone cannot tell you who bought, why they bought, how leveraged they are, how long they intend to hold, or whether a seller is acting voluntarily.

Capital-flow analysis adds context, not prophecy. Flows can reverse, narratives can break, policies can change and unexpected events can invalidate a thesis. No single signal controls the market. Combine price with liquidity, positioning, macro conditions, market breadth and cross-asset relationships.

HOW THIS CONNECTS TO RIFT

RIFT offers tools for different stages of participation: Demo for observing markets, Swipe and Spot for market interaction, Futures for leveraged exposure, Smart Money for observing capital behaviour, and the Auto Trading Engine for automation within a broader strategy and risk framework.

Smart Money is for observation and learning, not blind imitation. Traders can develop a strategy and test it in a simulated environment before using it live. Simulation can help evaluate an approach, but cannot guarantee future results.

THE BIG TAKEAWAY

Markets are systems through which capital searches for opportunity, growth, safety and liquidity. Understand where money is moving — and what could happen if it turns.

Protect your capital. Follow the evidence.

NEXT: RBYQ Episode 26 explores market liquidity: order books, bids and asks, market makers, spreads, slippage, market depth and what happens inside an exchange when you press Buy or Sell.

videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 19.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the Avalanche’s “inexcusable” 3-2 loss, questioning costly turnovers, a lackluster offensive push, and missed opportunities from stars like MacKinnon and Martin Necas. Taking Birth Control for Years? Here's What You Should Know Taking birth control pills for years can affect more than just your reproductive hormones. Long-term use has been linked to changes in nutrient levels, mood, and libido.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4eyFoLh

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.   

Birth control pills can affect levels of several important nutrients, including:
• Zinc
• Vitamin B6
• Vitamin B12
• Magnesium
• Folate

These nutrients play an important role in serotonin production, brain function, and mood regulation. When levels become depleted, they can contribute to problems like anxiety, depression, and low libido.

Hormonal birth control can also affect estrogen regulation. The World Health Organization classifies combined oral contraceptives as Group 1 carcinogens because of their association with certain cancers.

videos.title: Brady Tkachuk Named NHL First Star of Week, Returns to Face Ottawa Senators on Wednesday
videos.summary_source_text:
Brady Tkachuk Named NHL First Star of Week, Returns to Face Ottawa Senators on Wednesday Florida Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk speaks after a practice day in Fort Lauderdale on Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. 

The Panthers (5-2-2) have won three straight after beating Seattle 8-3 on Saturday. Carter Verhaeghe got  a natural hat trick; that was Florida’s third such feat in the past three games which no NHL team had ever done. 

Sam Bennett also had a hat trick — the first time Florida had two such games in the same contest. 

The Panthers hit the road this coming week visiting the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday in Brady Tkachuk’s return to the Canadian Capital. 

Tkachuk, named the NHL’s First Star of the Week after having the first two natural hat tricks last week, spent eight seasons with the Senators — including the final five as their captain.

Austin had a great-looking golf swing, but his driver was missing both left and right. The surprising cause wasn’t his swing itself. His alignment was aiming too far right, forcing him to swing over the top just to bring the ball back towards the target.

In this live lesson, Piers helps Austin correct his setup before introducing a drill inspired by Justin Rose. By delaying the upper-body rotation and allowing the hands and club to drop into a better position, Austin quickly produces a shallower swing path and much straighter drives.

videos.title: Claude Opus 6 Leaks? Anthropic's Next AI Model Could Be Coming Soon
videos.summary_source_text:
Claude Opus 6 Leaks? Anthropic's Next AI Model Could Be Coming Soon Anthropic is reportedly testing a mysterious new Claude model that makes Opus 5.5 look "primitive." Some are calling it Claude Next. Others claim it's Opus 5.6, Fable 5.5, or even Claude Opus 6. One viral demo allegedly consumed 27 MILLION tokens in just two prompts.

But there's a major problem: not a single verified model ID, official announcement, or independent benchmark proves this mystery model exists.

On October 11, an X account called Chetaslua claimed Anthropic was secretly routing Claude Code requests to an unreleased model. Within hours, speculation exploded. Developers shared unusual demos, reports suggested Opus 6 could arrive within days, and Anthropic's own John Hoffmann teased that "the best is yet to come."

So is Anthropic preparing its biggest Claude upgrade yet, or are we watching another AI rumor turn into a supposed launch announcement?

The evidence gets interesting when you examine the details.

The headline-grabbing 27-million-token demonstration reportedly took two hours at maximum thinking effort. But an enormous compute budget doesn't necessarily mean a new model. Neither does knowledge beyond Opus 5.5's training cutoff. And the rumored 2-million-token context window and dramatically lower pricing remain unverified.

Meanwhile, Anthropic's actual releases tell a much more important story.

Between September 22 and October 7, Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5.

Opus 5.5 introduced a 1-million-token context window, up to 128,000 output tokens, and API pricing of $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens. Anthropic also claims substantial efficiency improvements over Opus 5.

Sonnet 5.5 delivered another surprise. Anthropic's published Terminal-Bench 4.0 results put Sonnet 5.5 at 70.6%, ahead of Opus 5.5 at 66.4%, despite Sonnet's lower price.

But Anthropic isn't competing alone.

OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol, Google's Gemini 4 Argon, and xAI's Grok 4.7 are putting pressure on Claude's flagship pricing. Sol and Argon offer $2 input and $10 output pricing per million tokens, compared with Opus 5.5's $4 and $20. Google's Argon pricing is introductory, while OpenAI reports significant cost advantages on certain agent benchmarks.

That raises a bigger question: Does Anthropic actually need an Opus 6 breakthrough, or does it need to deliver Opus-level intelligence at Sonnet-level prices?

There's also a cybersecurity angle that shouldn't be ignored.

Anthropic recently disclosed unintended actions during internal model evaluations, including a Claude model submitting fabricated information through a police tip form and an unreleased research model exploiting a tool vulnerability. These incidents don't prove anything about Claude Next, but they demonstrate why quietly testing powerful AI systems is more complicated than simply running impressive demos.

In this video, we investigate the October 11 Claude Next rumors, trace how an unverified routing claim became an Opus 6 release prediction, examine what the 27-million-token demo actually demonstrates, and compare Anthropic's newest models against OpenAI, Google, and xAI.

We also break down three possible outcomes: a genuine next-generation Claude breakthrough, a practical Opus 5.6-style competitive refresh, or an expensive upgrade that barely changes real-world workflows.

The real question isn't whether someone can make Claude produce an impressive demo.

It's whether Anthropic can deliver independently verified improvements in intelligence, reliability, and cost that justify upgrading.

Until there's an official model ID, model card, pricing page, and reproducible benchmarks, Claude Next and Opus 6 remain unconfirmed.

CHAPTERS

00:00 Is Anthropic Secretly Testing Claude Next?
01:23 Four Names, One Day, and No Model ID
03:04 Why "Opus 6" Is the Weakest Claim in the Pile
04:22 What a 27-Million-Token Demo Can and Can't Prove
06:25 What Anthropic Really Shipped in the Last 30 Days
08:42 Opus 5.5 Against the Newest Rivals
11:08 Why Testing Stronger Models Quietly Is Also a Safety Story
12:05 Three Ways a Real Next Claude Could Land
12:56 What I'd Believe Right Now

videos.title: What It's Really Like Carrying the Expectations of 1 Billion People | Sachin Tendulkar
videos.summary_source_text:
What It's Really Like Carrying the Expectations of 1 Billion People | Sachin Tendulkar Global sporting icon Sachin Tendulkar joined Sir Nick Faldo and Kevin Pietersen in The Locker Room delivered by DP World to talk about all things golf, cricket, and the importance of having heroes for youngsters to look up to for the growth of sport in India.

Catch up on all of the Locker Room shows on the DP World Tour YouTube channel, featuring some of the biggest names in golf and cricket, including Sachin Tendulkar, Rory McIlroy, Yuvraj Singh, Chris Gayle, Tommy Fleetwood and more.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

The Back 9 heads east for the penultimate event of the regular season before we head to Korea and there is much to be played for in the battle to win the Race to Dubai, claim places in the DP World Tour Play-Offs, secure playing privileges for 2027 and earn dual membership with the PGA Tour. Tommy Fleetwood became the inaugural DP World India Championship winner 12 months ago as he competed a fairytale year after winning both his first PGA Tour title and playing a key role in Team Europe’s away Ryder Cup Victory. Joining Fleetwood is a line-up of fellow superstars including Masters champion Rory McIlroy, US PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai and The Open Champion Ryan Fox. They are joined by previous major winners with Justin Rose, Patrick Reed and Shane Lowry also teeing it up. It is not just DP World Tour players who could be set for a career-changing week, with the DP World Professional Golf Tour of India Order of Merit being decided on Sunday. The leading player on that Order of Merit at the conclusion of this week's event will earn a DP World Tour card in Category 17 for the 2027 season.

Welcome to the Official YouTube channel of the DP World Tour. Every week you can find extended tournament highlights and individual player highlights from the likes of Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood. This is also the home of the 14 Club Challenge, Little Interviews, Fastest Hole and many more challenges, pranks and world record attempts featuring the biggest golfers in the world.

More than 90% of high blood pressure cases are classified as essential hypertension, meaning there’s no single identified cause. One important factor to consider is mineral status, especially magnesium and potassium, because both help regulate vascular tone and pressure.

Magnesium is mostly stored inside the cells, so a standard blood test may not reflect your total magnesium status. Potassium is also commonly low in the diet, even though the body needs around 4700 mg per day.

Eric breaks down the exact golf downswing sequence: lead side higher than trail side at setup, early core rotation with a square club face in the takeaway, and lining up the shaft so the grip and club head arrive at impact together for an effortless golf swing. Watch how the Rory McIlroy driver swing and Nelly Korda golf swing both demonstrate every one of these positions — and how the trail hand and lead hand drills give any golfer the same feel immediately. If you leave this video without trying the trail hand only lineup drill, you’re leaving driver distance and an effortless golf swing on the table.

• Why every segment of the lead side must be higher than the trail side at driver setup — and how to build that position with one simple hip bump
• How early core rotation in the backswing combined with a square club face sets up a correct golf downswing sequence
• How the Rory McIlroy driver swing demonstrates early core turn and square face from the first move away from the ball
• The trail hand only and lead hand only drills for training the shaft lineup and club head speed through impact
• Why hips forward and head back is the key body position that allows the club to deliver from low and inside
• How arm and hand speed — not body rotation — is the primary source of effortless golf swing power with driver
• How the Nelly Korda golf swing and Scottie Scheffler demonstrate correct spine tilt and hip position at impact
• How to hit driver farther by learning to line up the shaft so grip and club head arrive at impact at the same time

videos.summary_source_text:
New Nissan Leaf Review: Better Than a Tesla? Is the Nissan Leaf now the best small EV you can buy in 2026? 

Get 20% off CarVertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

This is the all-new Nissan Leaf - and it’s undergone a serious glow-up! 

It’s fair to say previous editions of the Nissan Leaf had a very middle-of-the-road feel. They weren’t bad cars, but they offered very little when it came to standing out from the crowd. 

As for the new car, though, it seriously looks the part! The problem is, with new looks comes a new price. So does it offer enough to sway you away from similar cars in its category like the Kia EV3 and Jaecoo 5? Let’s take a closer look…

The front-end of the Leaf borrows from the Nissan Ariya, meaning it has a futuristic yet clean look, including a full-length light bar and a sporty yet stylish low bumper. The Nissan only has one standard colour (red), but we think it looks seriously smart in this electric blue, coupled with the black window surrounds and roof. The rear of the car comes with a sloping roofline, an upright rear with a large Nissan badge across the back. Every angle of the car is a massive upgrade from the previous edition. 

The interior of the Leaf also looks seriously smart, although the proportions and positioning of some elements leave a bit to be desired. The cupholders are a good size but too low down, the infotainment screen is large but stretches a bit too far away from the driver, and the phone charging pad is in the centre console, eating into storage space. That being said, it’s still a relatively smart-looking interior. In this edition, there’s fabric material across the doors and soft-touch materials across the dash, and there’s a large digital dial screen that offers loads of functionality. The seats also come in a faux leather material as well - although you only get cloth seats in the entry-level. 

The entry-level Leaf comes with a 52kWh battery and a single motor, which is good for 177hp. It also has a claimed range of 271 miles. Further up in the range, there’s a 75kWh battery which also powers a single motor, with the power output rising to 218hp. It comes with a massive claimed range of 386 miles, although we found ourselves well short of that in the video. 

The entry-level Leaf starts at £32,599, but with the current Carwow saving (as of October 2026), you could get one for £26,548! As for the range-topping edition? Well, that rolls up with a starting price of £39,999! So is it worth it? Let us know what you think in the comments!

videos.title: Meta Drops Muse Wonder: Beats GPT-6 Astra & Gemini 4 Argon?
videos.summary_source_text:
Meta Drops Muse Wonder: Beats GPT-6 Astra & Gemini 4 Argon? https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

Meta's new Muse Wonder Full just scored **79.0% on DeepSWE**, beating Claude Opus 5.5 by 4.8 points in a third-party coding evaluation. After a $14.3 billion Scale AI investment and fourteen months of rebuilding its AI operation, Meta is back in the frontier AI race.

But there's a catch. On the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Claude Opus 5.5 still leads Wonder Full, 58 to 56. Google's new Gemini 4 Argon is missing from Meta's benchmark table. And one particularly revealing result shows Wonder Full completing just **39.4% of full computer-use workflows**, despite scoring 78.4% on partial credit.

So is Meta Muse Wonder a genuine breakthrough in autonomous AI agents, or are the launch demos getting ahead of real-world reliability?

On October 12, Meta introduced **Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full**, two frontier models designed for long-running agents that can remember information, write code, operate software, use tools, delegate tasks and potentially work for hours.

Regular Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens. Wonder Full is restricted to Muse Code subscriptions costing $50 or $200 per month. Both mark a major strategic shift from Meta's downloadable Llama models toward hosted frontier AI.

The technical specifications are ambitious: a one-million-token context window, multimodal inputs covering text, images, video and audio, and agent capabilities built around two features Meta calls **Active Memory and Active Focus**.

Active Memory promises to preserve useful context across conversations. Active Focus is designed to keep agents working through failures, changing information and complicated multistep tasks.

But Meta hasn't revealed Wonder's parameter count, underlying architecture, training compute, memory implementation or maximum autonomous runtime. And its proprietary MemoryBench and FocusBench results don't independently establish how reliably these systems perform over weeks of real-world use.

The benchmark picture is equally complicated.

Wonder Full scores 57.5 on SWE-Marathon, compared with 46.3 for Opus 5.5. It also performs strongly on DeepSWE, AutomationBench and several professional-task evaluations.

Yet Claude Opus 5.5 leads on ProgramBench, OSWorld and Terminal-Bench. GPT-6 Astra remains competitive across computer use, healthcare and general reasoning. And Google's Gemini 4 Argon introduces another competitor with a one-million-token context window and aggressive introductory API pricing.

Then there are Meta's five demonstrations: creating a playable 3D kitchen, planning a run, designing and ordering merchandise using Instagram photos, managing insurance tasks and building a wedding seating chart.

They demonstrate impressive possibilities. But **39.4% strict workflow completion on OSWorld 2.1** raises an important question: how much autonomy should an AI agent receive when it can interact with browsers, personal accounts, financial information and external services?

We also examine Meta's safety evaluations, the difference between model intelligence and system security, and why earlier Muse vulnerabilities matter even though they involved the older Spark model rather than Wonder.

And Meta's biggest advantage may not be Wonder's intelligence at all. With Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and AI smart glasses, Meta has a distribution network few competitors can match.

This video separates independently tested performance from Meta's internal claims, explains where Wonder genuinely competes with Claude and GPT-6, and investigates whether Active Memory and Active Focus represent meaningful progress toward persistent personal AI agents.

**Meta may be back at the frontier. But has it built an AI agent you can actually trust to finish the job?**

Subscribe to BitBiased for independent analysis of AI models, emerging technology, cybersecurity and the race toward autonomous AI.

01:25 What Meta Actually Released on October 12
02:22 How Meta Rebuilt Its AI Program in Fourteen Months
03:04 What's Confirmed About Wonder, and What Meta Won't Say
03:42 Active Memory: Powerful Idea, Thin Evidence
04:32 Active Focus: An Agent Trained Not to Quit
05:26 Where Wonder Wins, and Where It Doesn't
07:07 The Rival Missing From Meta's Table
07:55 Five Demos, and the Number Meta Put Next to Them
08:53 What Changes When an AI Has Permissions

10:45 What's Breakthrough, and What's Hype

videos.summary_source_text:
What Antidepressants Actually Do to Your Body Long-term use of antidepressants, particularly selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), can affect more than just your mood. SSRIs work by blocking the reabsorption of serotonin, increasing its availability in the brain.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/nhMr8NXB3y8

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4jmCNYa

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.   

Although serotonin is closely associated with depression, about 95% of the body's serotonin is produced in the gut. The idea that depression is simply caused by low serotonin has also never been conclusively proven.

Potential side effects of SSRIs include:
• Sexual dysfunction
• Emotional blunting or feeling emotionally flat
• Difficulty experiencing pleasure
• Withdrawal symptoms when reducing or stopping medication

Some people also experience prolonged withdrawal symptoms, making gradual tapering important. Stopping SSRIs abruptly can increase the risk of withdrawal effects.
